title: Kenya Golf Safari for Your Club, With Four Great Courses, Two Mara Days and an Ocean Finish
meta_title: Kenya Golf Safari: Best Courses, Route and Group Costs
meta_description: Plan a Kenya golf safari for your club: Karen, Muthaiga, the Rift Valley and Vipingo Ridge, two Masai Mara days, best months and group logistics.
excerpt: A Kenya golf safari pairs Nairobi's classic courses, the Rift Valley and Vipingo Ridge with two days in the Masai Mara. Here is the route, season and group logistics for clubs.
content:
A Kenya golf safari pairs rounds on the country's best-known courses with game drives in the Masai Mara, usually over seven or eight days. The classic route plays Karen and Muthaiga in Nairobi, the Great Rift Valley course above Lake Naivasha and the PGA Baobab Course at Vipingo Ridge on the coast, with two Mara days in between.

Organising this for a club or a group of golfing friends is where it gets tricky: tee times at private clubs, golf bags on bush roads and light aircraft, non-golfers to keep happy and a budget everyone signs off. This guide sets out the courses, the route, the season and the group logistics, written by our Nairobi team, so you can plan your golf club safari in Kenya with fewer surprises.

Quick Facts

  • Ideal length: 7-8 days with four rounds and two full days in the Masai Mara
  • Core courses: Karen Country Club, Muthaiga Golf Club, Great Rift Valley Lodge and Golf Resort, PGA Baobab Course at Vipingo Ridge
  • Altitude: Nairobi courses sit at roughly 1,700-1,800 m; the Great Rift Valley course is at about 7,000 feet (about 2,130 m)
  • Best months: January-February and June-October (dry); July-October adds the Mara migration
  • Big event: The 2027 Magical Kenya Open is set for 18-21 February 2027 at Karen Country Club
  • Group size: Works from 4 golfers up to a full club group of 20+, with mixed golfers and non-golfers

What does a Kenya golf safari actually involve?

A Kenya golf safari is a private group trip that alternates golf days and wildlife days. Players usually get four rounds on four different courses, and the whole group shares a block of game drives in the Masai Mara, with a beach finish on the north coast if time allows.

The appeal of a Kenya golf safari is how close everything is. Nairobi has several championship courses within a short drive of each other, the Rift Valley course is about two hours north-west of the city, and the Mara and the coast are linked by scheduled light aircraft. You never spend a whole day travelling just to reach the next tee.

For a club, running the trip privately rather than joining a scheduled tour matters. Your group sets the tee times, keeps its own vehicles and guide, and can add a scored competition or a prize-giving dinner. Our group safaris are built this way: one itinerary, one quote, and travellers who can pay separately and arrive on different flights.

Which golf courses in Kenya belong on the trip?

The four courses most clubs choose for a Kenya golf safari are Karen Country Club, Muthaiga Golf Club, the Great Rift Valley Lodge course and the PGA Baobab Course at Vipingo Ridge. Together they give you two historic Nairobi layouts, a high-altitude resort course and a modern coastal championship course.

CourseWhere it isWhat stands out
Karen Country ClubKaren, south-west NairobiOpened in 1937, partly on Karen Blixen's former coffee estate; host of the 2027 Magical Kenya Open
Muthaiga Golf ClubMuthaiga, northern Nairobi, beside Karura ForestFounded in 1913 with an 18-hole course from 1926; a long-time Kenya Open venue
Windsor Golf Hotel and Country ClubNorthern Nairobi, among forest and coffeeOver 70 bunkers; a good alternative or extra Nairobi round
Sigona Golf ClubNear Kikuyu, north-west of NairobiOpened for play in 1938 at about 6,000 feet; a quieter, traditional parkland round
Great Rift Valley Lodge and Golf ResortEburru range above Lake Naivasha18 holes at about 7,000 feet, 6,580 yards, with lake and escarpment views
PGA Baobab Course, Vipingo RidgeKilifi County, under an hour north of MombasaPar 72, 6,586 yards, designed by David Jones; Africa's first PGA-accredited course

Nairobi's two classic rounds

Karen and Muthaiga are the heart of any Kenya golf safari. Karen Country Club dates from 1937, and shade trees from Blixen's coffee plantation still line parts of the course. Muthaiga, on the edge of Karura Forest, is a members' club, so we confirm visitor rounds with the club when we quote rather than promising a date.

Altitude is the first thing golfers notice on a Kenya golf safari. At around 1,700 m the ball carries noticeably further than at sea level, so most players club down for the first few holes. Morning tee times also avoid the stronger afternoon heat and any short afternoon showers.

The Rift Valley and the coast on a Kenya golf safari

The Great Rift Valley course is the round people talk about afterwards. It sits at about 7,000 feet on the Eburru range, with views over Lake Naivasha and Mount Longonot, and zebras have been seen crossing the fairways. The 17th, a par 5 of 598 metres, is the signature hole.

On the coast, the PGA Baobab Course at Vipingo Ridge is a 6,586-yard, par 72 layout set among baobabs, with giraffe, zebra, eland and oryx living on the estate. It also hosts the Magical Kenya Ladies Open. Two-seater buggies cost Ksh 3,300 for nine holes and Ksh 5,200 for 18 (checked November 2026), and the resort encourages every player to take a caddie.

How should the route run from Nairobi to the coast?

The smoothest Kenya golf safari route runs Nairobi, Lake Naivasha, Masai Mara and then the coast, ending with a flight home from Mombasa. It keeps road transfers short, puts the safari in the middle where the group is most rested, and saves the beach and the final round for last.

DayGolfSafari and travel
Day 1NoneArrive in Nairobi, transfer to Karen, welcome dinner
Day 2Karen Country ClubNon-golfers visit the Giraffe Centre or the elephant orphanage
Day 3Muthaiga Golf ClubDrive about 2 hours to Lake Naivasha
Day 4Great Rift Valley courseAfternoon boat ride on Lake Naivasha
Day 5NoneDrive about 5 hours to the Masai Mara, afternoon game drive
Day 6NoneFull day of game drives, optional balloon flight
Day 7NoneMorning drive, light aircraft to the coast, transfer to Vipingo Ridge
Day 8PGA Baobab CourseFinal round, transfer to Moi International Airport

This Kenya golf safari route is the shape of our 8 day Kenya golf safari, and it flexes easily. Short on time? Drop the coast and fly back to Nairobi from the Mara. Want more golf? Add Windsor or Sigona on a spare Nairobi morning. If the group would rather fly in both directions, the 2 day Masai Mara flying safari slots in as a short wildlife break between Nairobi rounds.

Lake Naivasha works as more than an overnight stop. Golfers play the Rift Valley course while others take a boat among hippos and fish eagles or walk in Hell's Gate, and our guide to Lake Naivasha lodges covers where else a group can stay nearby.

How much Masai Mara time do golfers need?

On a Kenya golf safari, golfers need two full days in the Masai Mara at minimum, which means three nights if you arrive by road and two if you fly in. That gives the group four or five game drives, enough for a good chance of lions, elephants, buffalo and, with luck, a leopard or cheetah.

From July to October the migration herds are usually in the Kenyan Mara, and river crossings are possible, though never guaranteed on a given day. Our guide to the Mara migration explains the timing month by month. Outside those months the resident wildlife is still excellent and camps are quieter.

Reserve fees are charged per person per day and differ by season and residency, so check the current rates in our Masai Mara entrance fee guide before you budget. The early balloon flight over the plains is a popular add-on for groups and is booked separately.

When is the best time for golf and safari in Kenya?

The best time for a Kenya golf safari is January to February or June to October, Kenya's two drier spells. Courses play firm and fast, roads to the Mara are easier, and game viewing is at its best. November brings short rains and March to May the long rains, which soften fairways and can close tracks.

January and February are warm and green, and the Magical Kenya Open is a natural anchor: the 2027 edition is set for 18-21 February at Karen Country Club, as announced by the DP World Tour in September 2026. Book flights and hotels early if your club wants to watch a round, because Nairobi fills up that week.

June to August is cool in Nairobi, often grey in the mornings, and ideal for walking 18 holes. July to October is migration season and the busiest, priciest period in the Mara, so book camps six to nine months ahead for a group. Our page on the best time to visit Kenya covers the weather month by month.

How are golf groups priced and organised?

Kenya golf safari groups are priced per person from five things: the number of travellers, room types, season, the courses chosen and whether you fly or drive between the Mara and the coast. Green fees and tee-time booking for the listed rounds are usually included, while club hire, caddies and buggies are paid locally.

Our group terms for a Kenya golf safari are simple. For every six paying travellers the seventh place is free, a deposit of 30 to 40% holds the booking and the balance is due two to four weeks before travel. Each traveller can pay separately. For a sense of wider safari budgets, our Kenya safari cost guide breaks down lodges and park fees by tier.

Vehicles, rooming and golf bags

Safari vehicles seat six or seven with a window seat each, but golf bags change the maths. For a Kenya golf safari group with full bags we plan one vehicle for every four or five golfers, or a separate luggage vehicle, so nobody rides with clubs on their lap. Twin rooms keep costs down, and single rooms are quoted per person.

Light aircraft from the Mara take soft bags only and have strict weight limits, so golf bags rarely fly. The usual fix is to send the clubs by road from Naivasha to the coast while the group flies, so they are waiting at Vipingo Ridge. Check visa and entry rules for every traveller too: our guide to the Kenya eTA explains what to apply for before you fly.

What do non-golfers do while the club plays?

Non-golfers on a Kenya golf safari have plenty to fill the golf mornings. In Nairobi they can feed giraffes at the Giraffe Centre, watch the orphaned elephants at feeding time or take a half-day drive in Nairobi National Park, all close to the Karen and Muthaiga courses.

At Naivasha, the stop most Kenya golf safari groups make next, the lake boat ride and Hell's Gate cycling are both done by lunch, and at Vipingo Ridge the beach and pool do the rest. The Mara days are shared by everyone, which is what makes a mixed group work: the golf divides the group in the mornings, and the safari brings it back together.

If your club wants to go further, the same model works across the region. We also run golf trips that combine Kigali with gorilla trekking, described in our Rwanda golf trip guide, and a Tanzania version built around the Serengeti golf course near Fort Ikoma.

Insider Tips

  • Lock Muthaiga first: Ask for private-club rounds as soon as dates are set, and keep a Windsor or Sigona round as the back-up
  • Play early: Book tee times between 7:00 and 9:00 for cooler air and firmer greens
  • Club down at altitude: Expect extra carry on the Nairobi and Rift Valley courses for the first few holes
  • Separate the bags: Send golf bags by road to the coast before the Mara flight
  • Take caddies: Local caddies read the greens well and caddie fees support training schemes at clubs such as Vipingo Ridge
  • Plan a prize night: A scored competition and dinner on the last evening gives the trip a proper finish

Frequently Asked Questions

How many days does a Kenya golf safari need?

A Kenya golf safari needs seven or eight days for most clubs. That covers two Nairobi rounds, a night or two at Lake Naivasha for the Rift Valley course, two full days of game drives in the Masai Mara and a final round on the coast at Vipingo Ridge.

Can visitors play Muthaiga Golf Club?

Visitors can usually play Muthaiga Golf Club, but it is a private members' club, so visitor rounds follow the club's own rules and tee times are confirmed only when your group is booked. A Kenya golf safari plans Muthaiga early in the week and keeps Karen Country Club or Windsor as the back-up round if the date is not available.

What is the best month for a Kenya golf safari?

The best months for a Kenya golf safari are January, February and June to October, when the weather is mostly dry. January and February are warm and pair well with the Magical Kenya Open, while July to October adds the wildebeest migration in the Masai Mara. The long rains from March to May are the wettest stretch for golf.

Should we bring our own golf clubs to Kenya?

Most serious golfers bring their own clubs to Kenya, and the main clubs and resorts also offer hire sets, caddies and buggies on request. The catch is the light-aircraft flight from the Masai Mara, which has strict soft-bag limits, so on a Kenya golf safari the golf bags usually travel by road to the coast while the group flies.

Is a Kenya golf safari suitable for non-golfers?

A Kenya golf safari suits mixed groups well, because the courses sit close to things non-golfers enjoy. While players are out, partners can visit the Giraffe Centre and the elephant orphanage in Nairobi, take a boat on Lake Naivasha or rest at the beach, and everyone shares the Masai Mara game drives together.

Final Thoughts

A Kenya golf safari works because the golf and the wildlife are so close together: two historic Nairobi rounds, a high round above Lake Naivasha, two days with the Mara's big cats and a coastal finish at Vipingo Ridge. Get the private-club tee times and the golf-bag logistics right, and the rest falls into place.
